title: Per-model dynamic outlier mapping & layer-scale correction for robust FP8/INT8 calibration
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: Reduce accuracy regressions caused by extreme per-layer activation outliers when applying FP8/INT8 quantization profiles. Deliver a per-model calibration workflow that: (1) detects and maps outlier sources by layer and head (attention/ffn), (2) computes corrective layer-scale factors and dynamic clipping thresholds, and (3) integrates fallback rules so production rollouts avoid user-visible quality drops. Focus models: LLaMA-family, Mistral variants, Qwen family. This ticket covers design, calibration harness changes, validation suites, CI checks, and runtime knobs for applying per-layer corrections during conversion and serving.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration harness produces stable per-layer scale factors for LLaMA-2-70B, Mistral-7B-v0.1, and Qwen-7B-Chat across 3 random prompt seeds

End-to-end INT8/FP8 conversion with new layer-scale corrections yields <= 1% loss in downstream generation quality metrics vs FP16 baseline on held-out eval prompts (measured by model-specific n-gram and reranker scores)
CI regression tests detect >0.5% drift in embedding cosine similarity or perplexity and block merge by default
Runtime supports applying per-layer fallback to FP16 or per-layer higher-precision kernels with a config flag; can be toggled per-model in stage and production
Documentation (Confluence) for the calibration recipe, and a reproducible GitHub notebook with sample calibrations and evals
technical_notes: Use percentile-based clipping (99.995th) per-channel for activations during calibration to avoid single-sample spikes dominating scale estimates
Compute both symmetric and asymmetric scale parameters; prefer asymmetric per-embedding/FFN outputs where activation distributions are skewed
Implement per-head attention activation monitoring: flag heads where tail mass > configured threshold and apply head-level scale factor or selective FP16 fallback
For Qwen variants, add special handling for wide FFN layers where we observed bimodal activation distributions; apply a two-stage calibration (global, then k-means bucketed per-activation magnitude)
LLaMA-family note: rotary/rotary-scaling interactions cause apparent outliers in early layers; adjust rotary scale compensation during calibration to avoid over-scaling later layers

Mistral note: sparse dense patterns in mixer blocks cause occasional large activations concentrated in a small set of channels; prefer clipping + additive noise during calibration to stabilize quantization bins
Store per-layer calibration metadata as compact vectors (quant_scale, zero_point, clip_percentile, fallback_reason) to be referenced by runtime without inflating model bundle size
Add kernel-selection metadata: if layer flagged for fallback, route to higher-precision kernel at runtime; ensure fallbacks are applied by policy rather than ad-hoc conversion changes
test_plan: Run calibration pipeline on curated 10k prompt calibration set (s3://redwood-quant/calib/10k-2026-03) for each target model
Measure metrics: generation BLEU-like n-gram scores on 2k eval prompts, embedding cosine drop on 5k sentence pairs, perplexity on held-out validation split
Ablations: (A) no layer-scaling baseline, (B) percentile clipping only, (C) layer-scale + clipping, (D) layer-scale + head-level fallback — compare accuracy/cost tradeoffs
Run latency and memory profiling for converted INT8/FP8 models including fallback layers to quantify 95th percentile token latency increase
Add unit tests in calibration harness to assert deterministic scale factor ordering for repeated runs with fixed RNG seed
Integrate nightly regression job that runs a smaller calibration+eval and posts results to perf dashboard; fail if metrics regress beyond thresholds
progress_updates: 2026-03-05: Spec drafted and reviewed with Research. Decided on percentile-based clipping + head-level monitoring as primary strategy.

2026-03-11: Qwen-7B calibration reveals bimodal FFN activations; experimenting with k-means bucketing in place of single global scale for those layers.

Add per-layer metadata serialization format and readpath in model bundle loader
Modify conversion tool to accept optional per-layer correction map and produce corrected FP8/INT8 params
Add runtime policy flags: quant.fallback.policy and quant.layer_corrections.enabled

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overfitting calibration to the calibration corpus causing regressions on production traffic. Mitigation: diversify calibration set (domains, prompt lengths) and use holdout validation; prefer conservative clipping percentiles by default

Risk: Increased bundle size and latency due to many per-layer fallbacks. Mitigation: compress metadata and prefer selective head-level fallback rather than whole-layer FP16; expose batch-aware fallback toggles
Risk: Hidden edge cases for new architectures. Mitigation: start with a small runway (canary models), monitor generation quality metrics and enable automated rollback on regression
Risk: Security review delays due to new metadata in bundles. Mitigation: flag ticket for security early and prepare threat model doc
notes_for_reviews: Please validate the proposed default clip percentile (99.995). Open to tuning but want a conservative default to reduce single-sample influence.
